title: People who frequently use ChatGPT for writing tasks are accurate and robust detectors of AI-generated text

model.params_source: paper footnote 22 (reasoning effort 'medium' for o1; temperature fixed at 1 by the API); max_completion_tokens assumed; max_tokens 4096 duplicates max_completion_tokens for the runner

task.subset_rule: all 300 annotated articles: 150 human-written + 150 AI-generated over Experiments 1-5 (30 + 30 each: GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GPT-4o paraphrased, o1-pro, o1-pro humanized)
task.approximation: the runner scores TPR only: items.filter keeps the 150 AI-generated articles (gold 'AI-generated' in the release, not 'Machine-generated'), so accuracy x 100 = TPR; the FPR half (150 human articles, gold HUMAN-WRITTEN) is a second run with the filter inverted

items.source: jenna-russell/human_detectors, file human_detectors.json (dict keyed by row index; fields generation_model, prompt_id, title, sub-title, author, source, issue, section, link, article, id, ground_truth ('Human-written' / 'Machine-generated'), annotator fields)
items.config_or_split: human_detectors.json, all 300 articles (five experiment batches identified by generation_model / evasion fields)
items.filter_prose: none (one record per article; annotator fields ignored)

prompt.user_template:
You are given a candidate text. Your task is to carefully read the candidate text and determine whether it was either written by a human or generated by AI.
Answer HUMAN-WRITTEN if the candidate text was likely written by a human.
Answer AI-GENERATED if the candidate text was likely generated by an AI.
<start of candidate text>{candidate_text}</end of candidate text>
<question>Is the above candidate text HUMAN-WRITTEN or AI-GENERATED? </question>
First, concisely describe the features of the candidate text that exemplify either AI or human writing. Then, provide your final answer.
<description> YOUR DESCRIPTION </description>
<answer> YOUR ANSWER </answer>
prompt.source_location: Table 20 'Prompt Template for the Zero-shot + CoT detector setup'
prompt.verbatim: full (PDF line wraps re-joined; 'Candidate Text' slot turned into a placeholder)

placeholders_prose.candidate_text: items.article (full article text) in place of the printed 'Candidate Text' slot

output.postprocess: strip, uppercase; missing label counted as HUMAN-WRITTEN (a miss for AI articles)
output.parse_prose: regex '<answer>\s*(HUMAN-WRITTEN|AI-GENERATED)\s*</answer>' (case-insensitive); fallback: last occurrence of either label

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: TPR = 100 x #(AI-generated articles labelled AI-GENERATED) / 150, reported with FPR = 100 x #(human articles labelled AI-GENERATED) / 150 (Table 2 cells are TPR (FPR))
metric.original_location: Table 2, section (C) prompt-based detectors, Detector LLM O1-2024-12-17, row Zero-shot + CoT, column Overall: 54 (4)

notes: Per-experiment TPRs (83.3, 53.3, 96.7, 20, 16.7) allow a batch-level check. human_detectors.json head verified (record 0: generation_model gpt-4o, article text present). Articles are ~1,000 words, so o1 calls cost about $0.10-0.20 each. human_detectors.json is a dict keyed '0'-'299'; each record carries its own 'id' field. Release ground_truth values: 'Human-written' / 'AI-generated'. || [triage 2026-09-09 g1] RUNNER DEFECT, not a deviation. items.jsonl has 61 distinct ids for the 150 articles: tierb_runner._parse_table flattens the dict-of-records as {'id': key, **record}, so the record's own non-unique 'id' field shadows the unique dict key; analyze()/battery.load_results key responses by (id, seed_idx), so 89 items were scored against another article's reply -> TPR 30.0 in result.json. Matching every item to its own call via sha_request (= sha256 of the request body; all 150 distinct) gives TPR 54.67 (82/150, CI 46.7-62.7; paper 54; original inside CI), per 30-article block in release order 80.0 / 96.7 / 56.7 / 23.3 / 16.7 vs the paper's per-experiment 83.3 / 53.3 / 96.7 / 20 / 16.7 (two middle batches swapped in order). Prompt = Table 20 verbatim, reasoning_effort medium = footnote 22, all 150 replies carry the <answer> tag. Corrected result: runs/tierb/W4406880877/result_sha_matched.json.
triage_note: 2026-09-09: duplicate item ids mis-paired replies; runner now forces unique ids and pairs archived calls by request hash. Re-analysis: TPR 54.67 [46.7, 62.7] (n=150) vs paper 54.
